title: Robins-Wood-Sheppard discrete gradient field for MSC arc geometry
description:
PATCH-29 v2 produces topologically correct MSC quad-cells but the arcs are traced by steepest-walk on the smoothed scalar, which gives 'non-convergent geometric embedding of separatrices' (Edelsbrunner) — arcs are short, zigzag, and don't actually cover the cell's face extent. Visual: large gaps between Coons reconstructions even though all faces are assigned.

The canonical fix is the Robins-Wood-Sheppard discrete gradient field (Theory and Algorithms for Constructing Discrete Morse Complexes from Grayscale Digital Images, IEEE TPAMI 2011). Pair simplices in lower stars via homotopy expansion; unpaired cells become critical points; V-paths through the gradient field replace steepest-walks. Result: arcs are combinatorially defined, topologically clean, and follow the surface properly.

Reference implementation: TTK (Topology ToolKit, https://github.com/topology-tool-kit/ttk) — its DiscreteGradient component is ~5000 LOC. We don't need full TTK; just the 2-manifold version with our existing critical-point set as input.

Unblocks: PATCH-29 v3 quality (arc-driven Coons reconstruction would actually cover cells); PATCH-27 refinement (cell-internal sub-MSC needs proper gradients); PATCH-32 per-tooth detection (better discrete gradient might separate adjacent tooth tips that smoothing-based extrema can't).
definition-of-done: 1. New DiscreteGradient.java implements lower-star pairing per RWS 2011. 2. MorseSmaleComplex.compute optionally consumes the discrete gradient instead of running its own classifier. 3. MSC arcs traced via V-paths through the gradient — verified by inspecting arc lengths (currently ~5 mesh hops per arc, expect 50+ on Skull.obj). 4. Coons reconstruction renders coverage ≥80% of mesh face area (currently ~30% by visual estimate).
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: a synthetic 8×8 grid with one Gaussian bump produces 1 max + 4 mins + 4 saddles, gradient field has no spurious critical points. 2. Run on Skull.obj; arc-length p50 increases from current ~5 to >25. 3. Visual: ms-coons-composite.png shows minimal gaps between cells. 4. p95 Coons error drops below the current 0.277 threshold approach.

References:
- Robins-Wood-Sheppard, IEEE TPAMI 2011: https://people.physics.anu.edu.au/~vbr110/papers/RWS_TPAMI.pdf
- Wikipedia Discrete Morse Theory: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Morse_theory
- TTK reference impl: https://github.com/topology-tool-kit/ttk
